kernel_of_truth.description: The daily re-fire is not a spurious signal about the underlying change — it is honest audit-lifecycle plumbing. The dispatcher (monitor/scripts/compute-curmudgeon-dispatcher-state.js:254) correctly filters by change.audited_at, and nothing writes that field. Yesterdays audit (REACTIVE-AUDIT-2026-07-16.json) explicitly recommended "if a fourth re-visit fires on 2026-07-17 with identical result, consider whether tinker can prioritize ISS-2986 to break the loop" — and tinkers own 2026-07-16 summary (last line) already commits ISS-2986 as its next pick. The loop is on-track to self-terminate in 1-2 cycles.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Even a well-behaved loop is non-zero Opus cost. Todays cheap consolidation confirms zero new information vs 07-16 — but if tinker keeps deferring past 07-17 (e.g., a fresh higher-severity ISS arrives), curmudgeon may want to escalate: (a) push a human-note asking operator to shift the audited_at gate to a REACTIVE-AUDIT-file scan (Option a from ISS-2986 description), or (b) manually re-run compute-curmudgeon-dispatcher-state.js with a debug flag to confirm the 7-day window is the only remaining brake. For now, letting the natural cadence run is correct.
